items.causalEvidenceSummary: Established monogenic CADASIL gene; this paper adds new data: a novel p.C533S mutation in a family, plus CRISPR knock-in in human brain microvascular endothelial cells. The knock-in reproduced CADASIL-like pathology (tight junction loss, inflammation, neuronal ferroptosis, glial activation) through VEGF/VEGFR pathway impairment. No GWAS or MR evidence.
items.sourceQuote: We reported a novel mutation in the exon 10 of the NOTCH3 gene (NOTCH3 p.C533S) in a Chinese family with CADASIL.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Known gene behind monogenic CADASIL. This paper adds new functional data: the CADASIL mutants R90C, C212Y and C455R are taken up into the cell, and the ectodomain separates inside endosomes (also seen in hESC-derived VSMCs). R90C shows gain-of-function, ligand-independent signalling through a TRPML-dependent, metalloprotease-independent route, which may explain ectodomain build-up in CADASIL. Cell-model evidence only; no GWAS, MR or omics data.
items.sourceQuote: R90C showed significantly increased signalling activity compared to WT and shifted to an alternative mechanism of activation that was independent of metalloprotease activity and dependent on TRPML, a calcium channel protein involved in endosomal/lysosomal fusion and fission.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Monogenic cSVD gene (CARASIL/CADASIL2). The review cites common intronic variant associations with extreme cSVD MRI markers and lacunar stroke, and an MTAG locus (HTRA1-ARMS2). Rare variants in UK Biobank are linked to stroke and vascular dementia. Review-level evidence (prior studies).
items.sourceQuote: Specifically, a common intronic variant in HTRA1 was shown to be associated with a combination of MRI markers of extreme cSVD (including the presence of lacunes and extensive WMH) in population-based cohorts (), and lacunar stroke in patient-based cohorts ().

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Monogenic cSVD gene. Common variants at the COL4A1-COL4A2 locus are associated with WMH, non-lobar ICH and lacunar stroke, and COL4A2 is an MTAG locus for lacunar stroke/WMH. Cited prior evidence.
items.sourceQuote: Likewise, common variants near the COL4A1-COL4A2 locus were found to be associated with WMH burden (, ), non-lobar ICH (), and lacunar stroke ().

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Monogenic hemorrhagic cSVD gene with extensive mouse model functional data (TGF-beta/PI3K, Notch3-driven ACT-zone hypermuscularization causing ICH). Common variants at the COL4A1-COL4A2 locus are associated with WMH, non-lobar ICH and lacunar stroke.
items.sourceQuote: Likewise, common variants near the COL4A1-COL4A2 locus were found to be associated with WMH burden (, ), non-lobar ICH (), and lacunar stroke ().

items.causalEvidenceSummary: CADASIL gene. Population sequencing data (UK Biobank) show cysteine-altering NOTCH3 variants are common and associated with increased stroke and vascular dementia risk. Endpoint is general stroke rather than a cSVD-specific phenotype.
items.sourceQuote: Despite apparently not causing classical CADASIL these mutations are nevertheless associated with an increased risk of stroke and vascular dementia in the general population ().

items.causalEvidenceSummary: At the lacunar stroke GWAS locus ICA1L-WDR12-CARF-NBEAL1. Supported by TWAS/colocalization (genetically elevated expression) and by integrated GWAS-proteomic analysis as a causal protein for lacunar stroke.
items.sourceQuote: By combining analysis of GWAS and proteomic data from lacunar stroke, three proteins (ICA1L, CAND2, ALDH2) felt to be causally related to disease pathogenesis were identified ().

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Lacunar stroke GWAS locus, with TWAS/colocalization support from genetically elevated expression associated with lacunar stroke.
items.sourceQuote: Such approaches identified association of genetically elevated expression of SLC25A44, ULK4, ICA1L, FAM117B, CARF, NBEAL1, with lacunar stroke ().

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Sole gene named at a genome-wide significant lacunar stroke GWAS locus in MRI-confirmed cases.
items.sourceQuote: Using such a more rigorous phenotyping approach in 7338 cases, 5 loci for lacunar stroke were identified (ICA1L-WDR12-CARF-NBEAL1, ULK4, SPI1-SLC39A13-PSMC3-RAPSN, ZCCHC14, ZBTB14-EPB41L3), and a further 7 identified on multitrait analysis with WMH (SLC25A44-PMF1-BGLAP, LOX-ZNF474-LOC100505841, FOXF2-FOXQ1, VTA1-GPR126, SH3PXD2A, HTRA1-ARMS2, COL4A2)().

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Sole gene label of an MTAG locus for lacunar stroke with WMH; also cited as a matrisome-associated gene linked to sporadic cSVD.
items.sourceQuote: Using such a more rigorous phenotyping approach in 7338 cases, 5 loci for lacunar stroke were identified (ICA1L-WDR12-CARF-NBEAL1, ULK4, SPI1-SLC39A13-PSMC3-RAPSN, ZCCHC14, ZBTB14-EPB41L3), and a further 7 identified on multitrait analysis with WMH (SLC25A44-PMF1-BGLAP, LOX-ZNF474-LOC100505841, FOXF2-FOXQ1, VTA1-GPR126, SH3PXD2A, HTRA1-ARMS2, COL4A2)().

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Only genome-wide significant locus in a cerebral microbleed GWAS meta-analysis (25,862 participants).
items.sourceQuote: There have been fewer studies of CMB largely because large data sets are not available due to the need for visual identification on MRI scans; a recent meta-analysis in 25,862 participants of whom 3556 had CMB, suggested significant heritability for this phenotype but only identified one gene at genome wide significance, the Apolipoprotein E locus ().

items.causalEvidenceSummary: This case report finds a pathogenic heterozygous NOTCH3 c.505C>T (p.Arg169Cys) variant in a CADASIL patient with confluent WMH and multiple subcortical infarcts after COVID-19. A skin biopsy showing granular osmiophilic material (GOM) in the vascular smooth muscle cell basement membrane confirms the diagnosis. NOTCH3 is an established monogenic cause of cSVD; the evidence here is a single new case, not a statistical association.
items.sourceQuote: Genetic analysis of NOTCH3 identified a heterozygous c.505C＞T (p.Arg169Cys) variant ( NM_000435.3 ), which is classified as pathogenic in ClinVar.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Case report of a newly genetically diagnosed CADASIL patient carrying a pathogenic NOTCH3 variant in EGFr domain 4. This is new clinical-genetic evidence for the established monogenic cSVD gene, with an atypical, mainly psychiatric presentation. There is no GWAS, omics or MR evidence.
items.sourceQuote: We report on a genetically newly diagnosed 63-year-old patient with cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL) with a two-decade course of severe affective symptoms in the absence of classical somatic disease characteristics although we found a pathogenic variant in the EGFr 4 domain of the NOTCH3 protein.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Established monogenic cause of CADASIL (hereditary cSVD). This paper presents new functional data: a light-chain split luciferase (LSL) assay discriminates pathogenic from benign NOTCH3 EGF-repeat variants (100% sensitivity, 93% specificity) and implicates abnormal disulfide bonding/thiol reactivity in both cysteine and non-cysteine CADASIL mutations. Cysteine alkylation rescued the defects. No GWAS or MR data.
items.sourceQuote: We demonstrate that LSL is capable of clearly differentiating benign from pathogenic changes in NOTCH3 using three parameters that result from luciferase measurements.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: GLA is the established monogenic gene for Fabry disease, which is linked to cSVD. This paper presents new variant data: four novel GLA mutations (p.G261C, c.786G>T/p.W262C, c.583insGAATA, p.Y207X) were found by Sanger sequencing in families, with reduced α-Gal A activity and raised Lyso-Gb3. The cSVD link is only clinical (TIA, retinal vessel tortuosity, stroke at diagnosis); the paper has no neuroimaging or cSVD-specific phenotyping.
items.sourceQuote: The proband was a 51-year-old woman with modest proteinuria and albuminuria and suspected cardiovascular damage; the woman showed conduction defects, tortuosity of the retinal blood vessels, hypertension, and a TIA (transient ischemic attack) event.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Case report of a novel truncating GLA variant (c.484delT, p.W162Gfs*3) causing classic Fabry disease, confirmed by very low enzyme activity and high Lyso-Gb3. The heterozygous female proband had ischemic microvascular white matter lesions/leukoencephalopathy on brain MRI; the hemizygous son's brain MRI was unremarkable. This is new variant-level data for an established monogenic cSVD gene, but only from case observation, with no statistical or population-level analysis.
items.sourceQuote: Brain MRI highlighted findings of an ischemic microvascular nature both in the white matter of frontal subcortical, parietal subcortical, periventricular, and in the cerebellar hemispheres.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Cis-pQTL MR exposure: genetically lower plasma APOE was associated with ≥2 SVD imaging markers (white matter damage and CMB), and colocalized (PP.H4>0.8). It was also linked to dementia in UKB-PPP. This is MR-exposure evidence, not a direct GWAS hit.
items.sourceQuote: Consistent with the prior study, 33 we found reduced plasma APOE levels were associated with white matter damage, CMBs, and increased risk of all-cause dementia independent of APOE genotypes (Figures 2 A and 4 A).

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Cis-pQTL MR: higher plasma EPHA2 was associated with white matter damage. The exact white matter marker is not specified in the main text. Colocalized (PP.H4>0.8), replicated, and consistent with dementia/stroke epidemiology. MR-exposure/drug target (TKIs).
items.sourceQuote: We found the most consistent evidence for EPHA2 and APOE with the support of both MR and conventional epidemiological analyses (Figure 5 A).

items.causalEvidenceSummary: This review links NOTCH3 to cSVD as the established monogenic cause of CADASIL, the most common hereditary cSVD. It pulls together data from several cohorts linking specific variants (p.R544C, p.R75P) to ICH risk, which is mostly deep (non-lobar) but sometimes lobar, and to microbleeds. NOTCH3 mutation carriers with ICH had more severe deep WMH, more basal ganglia perivascular spaces, more lacunes and more microbleeds than people with sporadic ICH. The evidence is a synthesis of earlier studies, not new genome-wide data.
items.sourceQuote: In conclusion, this review provides focused insights into ICH in CADASIL, highlighting considerable variability in ICH prevalence influenced by ethnic factors and specific NOTCH3 mutations, such as p.R544C and p.R75P.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Whole exome sequencing of 50 NOTCH3-negative suspected CADASIL patients found three likely causative mutations in collagen type IV genes. The abstract doesn't say whether COL4A1 or COL4A2 was affected, so confidence is moderate. The evidence is rare monogenic variants in clinically suspected cSVD, not GWAS.
items.sourceQuote: This analysis identified three mutations affecting the Collagen type IV genes in three individuals likely to be causative of CSVD.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Whole exome sequencing of 50 NOTCH3-negative suspected CADASIL patients found three likely causative mutations in collagen type IV genes. The abstract doesn't say whether COL4A1 or COL4A2 was affected, so confidence is moderate. The evidence is rare monogenic variants in clinically suspected cSVD, not GWAS.
items.sourceQuote: This analysis identified three mutations affecting the Collagen type IV genes in three individuals likely to be causative of CSVD.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Known monogenic cause of CADASIL, a cerebral small vessel disease. This study adds new genotype-phenotype data from 395 French CADASIL patients: pathogenic variant location in EGFr domains 1-6 was associated with an early-onset, rapidly progressing clinical subgroup. This is monogenic or clinical-progression evidence, not GWAS or MR.
items.sourceQuote: Male sex, lower education level, hypertension, and NOTCH3 pathogenic variant location within epidermal growth factor-like repeat (EGFr) 1-6 were found to be associated with this group difference.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Known monogenic cause of Fabry disease, which has cSVD features. This case series adds new data: a novel GLA missense variant (c.122C>G, p.Thr41Ser), reclassified as likely pathogenic under ACMG, in two unrelated patients with non-classic Fabry disease and mainly neurological involvement (ischemic strokes; periventricular, subcortical and juxtacortical white matter lesions). Evidence is clinical and case-level only (no GWAS or functional data). One patient's stroke was large-vessel (MCA), and the white matter lesions resembled MS.
items.sourceQuote: We identified two novel GLA variants c.50_54del and c.122C>G.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Known monogenic cause of CADASIL. This paper adds new genotype–phenotype data from 1,908 CADASIL-cohort cases and 101 UK Biobank carriers of cysteine-altering NOTCH3 variants: the NOTCH3-SVD stages (based on deep white matter hyperintensities, lacune count and mRS) were associated with PSMD, ischemic stroke, brain atrophy and cognition. High-risk variants reached higher stages at younger ages than moderate-risk variants. This is direct variant-carrier evidence, not GWAS or MR.
items.sourceQuote: Stratification based on NOTCH3 variant risk category illustrated that cases with a high-risk NOTCH3 variant had a higher estimated probability of meeting the criterion for a certain stage at a younger age than cases with a moderate-risk NOTCH3 variant ( Figure 5 C and D).

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Case report of a CADASIL patient carrying a heterozygous NOTCH3 Arg153Cys mutation in exon 4. She had rapidly progressive disease with repeated ischemic strokes, extensive WMH, microbleeds and brain atrophy. The paper also summarizes 14 patients with the same mutation. This is new clinical and variant data for an established monogenic cSVD gene, not a background citation.
items.sourceQuote: Here, we report a rare 50-year-old woman who had rapid disease progression with c.457C>T, p.Argl53Cys heterozygous mutation in exon 4 of NOTCH3 and discuss the possible reasons.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Established monogenic cause of CADASIL. This prospective cohort of 555 people with cysteine-altering NOTCH3 mutations adds new genotype–phenotype data. Mutations in EGFr domains 1–6 independently predicted earlier first stroke, which was almost always lacunar (HR 1.64, p=0.004), but did not significantly predict dementia. This is new population-level variant evidence, not a background citation.
items.sourceQuote: All patients had cysteine-altering NOTCH3 mutations; 433 (78.0%) were in EGFr domain 1–6.

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Established monogenic cSVD gene (CADASIL). This paper reports new data from Notch3 R169C mutant mice: lower FA, less MBP staining in the striatum and corpus callosum, microglial activation where myelin has changed, and focal extravascular IgG/fibrinogen, all resembling white matter changes in human SVD. The evidence is from an animal model only; there is no new human genetic association.
items.sourceQuote: Lower FA values, indicating myelin defects, were detected only in hypertensive BPH/2J and Notch3 mutant (CADASIL) mice at 6 months (Figure 1B,D ).

items.causalEvidenceSummary: Established monogenic cause of haemorrhagic SVD. Col4a1 G498V mutant mice showed microhaemorrhages on T2 MRI (confirmed by IgG staining), activated microglia at the haemorrhage sites and focal BBB leakage, but no white matter or myelin defects at 6 months. The evidence is from an animal model only.
items.sourceQuote: Six‐month‐old Col4a1 mutant mice showed hypointense signals in T2 maps in the interbrain region (Figure S3A ), indicating microhaemorrhages.
